text.p: Turkish central bank heavily funded banks on Friday to meet increased cash demand ahead of the weekend, bankers said.
The bank lent 63 trillion overnight at 80 percent on the interbank, up sharply from the 44 trillion lira it injected on Thursday. Overnight money also traded at 79.75 percent.
The money market opened 25.7 trillion lira short and banks' cash needs for the weekend further raised demand in the day.
The lira closed firmer at 101,800 against the dollar versus Thursday's 101,850.
Dealers said dollar demand eased on tightening liquidity after being relatively firm in the last two days.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory forex transfers at 101,550 lira at the opening, down from Thursday's 101,600 lira close, but raised it to 101,700 at close, in line with fluctuations in the dollar/mark parity.
Yields on t-bills and bonds firmed. They had stabilised on Thursday after diving in the first half of the week.

The average yield on the most heavily traded June 4, 1997 paper edged higher to 117.48 from Thursday's 117.05. The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 117.42, up sligthly from yesterday's 117.06 percent average.
